rubric.result: Every sentence of `### Desired end state` is delivered by the sum of the eight commits, and no promise is delivered by one commit and undone by a later one. (1) `POST /review-plan` is no longer routed: `api-server.ts` loses both the `app.post` and the `app.all` for `ReviewPlanRoute.PATH`, so the path falls to `Failures.nothingMatched`, and `api-server.test.ts:1317` plus `ct-api-real-process.test.ts:439` pin the 404 `{code:'not-found'}` in the test server AND in the real process; `review-plan-route.ts`, `ask-plan-changes.ts`, `review-plan.ts`, `read-changes-asked.ts`, `review-gate-policy.ts` and `CtApi.#planReviews` are deleted, and `frontend/src/app/review-plan/**` returns no file at all (Glob, empty). (2) The vocabulary is two members on both sides of the wire: `plan-state.ts` is `'writing' | 'ready'` with two constants, `ReadPlanProgress.#stateOf` is now `this.planProgress.of(...)` and nothing else, and `PlanEvents.frameFor(state: PlanStateValue)` (plan-events-route.ts:146) is the only writer of the frame's `state`; the frontend declares the same two in `PlanEvents.types.ts` and `usePlanProgress`, and `PlanProgress.tsx` lost `REWORKING_MESSAGE`, `onReviewing` and its effect. (3) `gatesForType` is `return TYPE_GATES[typeof type === 'string' ? type.trim() : ''] ?? []`, so no `Tipo` implies the gate while a row that writes `plan` in its `Gate` column still gets it (`resolveGates('backend','plan')` keeps it). (4) The surviving watch is intact: `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews` is context-only in the diff, `ReadFixesAsked`/`RequestFixes`/`PlanAgents.fix`/`ReviewWatch.start|startRecovered|stop` all stand, and only `refresh()` left. (5) `API.md` names the retired endpoint nowhere: the `## POST /review-plan` section, the `reviewing` frame with its paragraph and the `plan-under-review` row with its four paragraphs are gone, and the seven surviving sections count 2 POST + 5 GET, which is what the 'Reaching it' table now says (it said `7 (POST 3, GET 4)` over eight endpoints before, so the breakdown was corrected rather than left stale). (6) The observability bullet holds: no production line of the diff adds a log, a print or a counter (the only `+` lines matching `console.|process.std|stderr(` in the whole accumulated diff are inside the committed verdict JSONs and the metrics jsonl). Declared debt, read and endorsed rather than counted as a gap: `ReviewLog.lastAskedAt` and `MemoryReviewLog` survive with a writer (`ReviewWatch.#note`) and no production reader once `ReadPlanProgress.#underReview` left — `ct-api.ts:320` still builds `log: new MemoryReviewLog()` inside the protected `#pullRequestReviews`. That is a `simplicity.md` burden ('a public symbol, a parameter or a default with no caller'), and `simplicity.md` itself provides the escape used here: 'Where the burden cannot be discharged, that is declared in the task's report... and the decision is left to a person.' It is declared twice, in `### Out of scope` and in §9 assumption 4, with the reason the issue protects. Same reading for `GATES.plan.kickoff`'s «implicado por defecto en TODO slice»: the gate's operative instruction is still true for a row that asks for it, only the parenthetical about how it got there is not, and D-14 — a closed decision of §2 — binds the slice to not touching the distributed plugin beyond that single line. Reopening either would be reopening a closed decision, not judging an end state.

Eight commits, read in order against the eight `**Objective:**` lines: each leaves standing what the ones before it established, and every reversal among them is one a later task's objective asked for. The route leaves the backend (1) before its client leaves the page (2), which is the `conventions/decisions.md` pairing the plan's §2 row 'Where the two halves of a contract move together' promised — and the same pairing holds for `plan-under-review` (backend and frontend both in 3) and for `reviewing` (backend and frontend both in 6). Two intermediate scaffolds exist and both are retired by the task whose objective named them: `backend/__tests__/reviews-spy.ts` is trimmed in task 3 and deleted in task 4 ('nothing starts a watch over the plan's issue any more'), and `Home.planReviewing` survives task 2 — which is what task 2's own verdict flagged as a coverage gap 'worth knowing before task 6' — and is removed in task 6 ('`reviewing` leaves the plan state on both sides of the wire'). Nothing is solved twice: task 5's `PlanStatusFailure`/`PlanStatusNotRead`/`PlanStatusNotUnderstood` (the replacement family for `statusOf`, whose old family the same task deleted) is still the only one in `gh-plan-issues.ts` at the end, and no later task reintroduces `PlanChangesFailure`. The one reversal that happened inside the slice was contained in its own commit: task 7's first pass added `gate: 'plan'` to `PlanIssueBody.rowFor()` and reverted it, and the accumulated diff confirms it left no residue — `backend/src/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.ts` carries only task 5's `-REVIEW` removal and no `gate` line at all. Task 5's amendment to `git-workspace.ts` (dropping the `-REVIEW` invitation from `SliceSeed.GATES`) stays consistent with what the slice leaves routed: the seed still says a person closes the plan gate from the app, and `POST /implement-plan` is explicitly kept by `### Out of scope` until slice #6.

The declared signal — «a groom of any spec creates no `gate:plan` label and the plan stream emits only writing and ready» — is honoured by production lines of the accumulated diff, one half each, and the three checks hold. **Production emits it.** Half one is `plugin/scripts/gates.js#gatesForType`, whose production `return` is the line this slice changed; it is what `resolveGates` (gates.js:282) and `gatesForAgent` (gates.js:342) compute from, what `groom.js#buildLabels` turns into labels and what `ct-groom.mjs#labelReportLine` prints as `new labels ... in <repo>: ...` (ct-groom.mjs:1212), besides the `--dry-run` plan's `issues[].labels` and the labels `gh` actually puts on the issue. Half two is `PlanEvents.frameFor(state: PlanStateValue)` (plan-events-route.ts:146-148), the only writer of the stream's `state` field, fed by `ReadPlanProgress` over a `PlanState` the diff narrowed to two members; the narrowing is in production files (`plan-state.ts`, `read-plan-progress.ts`), not in a fixture or a mock. Neither half lives only in a test. **With the repo's own instrumentation.** Both channels were already on disk before this slice — the groom's own stdout report and the SSE frame the cabin's `usePlanProgress` consumes — and the slice brings no library, no emitter and no new line: grepping the whole accumulated diff for added `console.`/`process.stdout`/`process.stderr`/`stderr(` lines returns matches only inside the committed verdict JSONs and `docs/superpowers/metrics/issue-326.jsonl`, never in `backend/src`, `frontend/src` or `plugin/scripts`. The slice in fact removed an emit site (`implement-plan-route.ts`'s 'admitted the go ... without being able to read' warning) rather than adding one. **Every label is bounded.** The gate labels are a closed vocabulary (`gate:visual|apply|plan|none`) and the frame carries exactly one field, `state`, over a two-member enum; no issue number, timestamp, agent handle or free text enters either dimension. No smell: the signal is checkable by the suite (`gate-plan.test.js`, `read-plan-progress.test.ts:60`), which is the smell's first half, but its second half fails — what the cell names does not end with that run, since both a `gate:` label on a real issue and a `data: {"state":...}` frame are read in production after the merge, by the dispatcher and by a person on GitHub for the first and by the cabin's plan-progress panel for the second.

findings.what: The «known residue, left on purpose» that `### Out of scope` declares is three sites, not the one sentence it names. Besides `GATES.plan.kickoff`, two more comments still assert the retired default as present tense: `dispatch-check.mjs:995` and `go-response.js:73`, the latter saying outright «that is not a pending hole: it is today's hole». Both files are named by the same `### Out of scope` paragraph as debt A-3 modules, so the declaration covers them in substance and this changes nothing about the slice's delivery — `gatesForType` no longer hands the gate out and no code path reads these comments. It is recorded here only because a per-task judge could not see it (task 7 changed the behaviour; no task's `**Files:**` names either file) and because whoever sweeps A-3 will want the full list. Not a defect the slice owed: the same D-14 clause quoted in the plan — «so that this one can be built without touching the distributed plugin beyond that single line» — is what leaves all three standing.
